correctness.rationale: Reconstructed normalized Fourier inversion and real-conjugate pairing on C5. Independently computed the five Fourier coefficients of f² by cyclic convolution and confirmed ∥f∥4^4=6r^4+24r²s²+6s^4+8r³s cos(3α+β)+8rs³ cos(α−3β), with the latter rs³ term changing sign for Hf. The phase map (α,β)↦(3α+β,α−3β) has determinant −10 and is surjective on the two-torus, so both cosine variables can attain −1 independently; direct quotient partial derivatives then prove the global phase maximum. For t=s/r, exact symbolic differentiation independently yields R′(t)=−8t²(3t⁴−12t²+8t−9)/D(t)²; g is strictly negative on (0,1] and strictly convex on [1,∞), with g(1)<0 and g→∞, giving one positive stationary root t*=1.853258098625306… and global maximum X*=2.089689004569992… (∥H∥4≈1.202320949439024). Independently confirmed exact polynomial elimination 3185X⁴−17948X³+42750X²−47500X+15625, factor divisible by g(t)², and all ten phase solutions modulo 2π; the ten are one orbit under sign and five translations, so all real extremizers as stated. Cases r=0 or s=0 give quotient 1, below X*. The special C3 zero-mean fourth-moment identity also follows algebraically. This is an analytic proof, not an extrapolation from finite tests.
residual_risks: No external Lean or expert attestation is claimed; finite numerical checks are corroborative only.
Norm and extremizer classification are for real zero-mean C5 under the explicitly stated multiplier; no complex-input or arbitrary-N conclusion is proved.

evidence: Bañuelos–Kwaśnicki Theorem 1.1 settles the norm of the infinite-lattice transform on ℓp(Z), which is a different infinite-domain operator and not an exact finite C5 quotient norm.
The cyclic endpoint theorem and Riesz parity-block theorem explicitly restrict sharp norms to p=1 or p=∞, and so do not determine the p=4 operator norm here.
The four-state cyclic convolution theorem is uniformly in real C4 and does not dominate C5.
The finite-abelian co-singleton Λ(4) result gives an L2→L4 sharp synthesis norm, not the ratio between L4 norms before and after this sign multiplier.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Tested infinite-lattice bounds and finite cyclic all-order endpoint formulas for specialization, interpolation, duality or reduction. Endpoint Riesz–Thorin or convexity yields inequalities only, not the exact C5 norm and complete extremizer orbit; no inspected stronger parameter theorem dominates this claim.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality. Multiple semantic and exact-fingerprint searches of published Resultary findings, direct full-text comparisons of the closest cyclic Hilbert endpoint/parity and finite Fourier/L4 findings, and materially read original discrete Hilbert/finite-DFT sources found no prior claim that implies the exact real C5 L4→L4 norm and unique equality orbit. The finite-cyclic p=1,∞ theorem covers the same operator but a different exponent; the sharp infinite-lattice ℓp result is not a finite-C5 quotient; and the same-group co-singleton Λ(4) theorem optimizes another ratio. This remains bibliographic best-of-knowledge, not a novelty certificate.
residual_risks: Older finite-signal or discrete harmonic analysis studies may tabulate the same five-point L4 operator norm using another transform convention or terminology; no such equivalence was located in inspected sources.
The 1969 original scan had unread pages and no reliable textual search; inspected relevant construction and kernel pages yielded no claim of this exact norm.

The recently indexed arXiv:2610.10158 sharp Schatten/Hilbert transform paper was inspected at abstract-level only after full-text retrieval returned a block; its advertised domain is distinct, and it is not treated as an exhaustive negative source.
Some search hits were available only as short summaries; their titles/abstracts alone do not justify a whole-document NOT_COVERING finding.

value.rationale: The real cyclic Hilbert sign-multiplier p4 operator norm is a natural finite version of a classical harmonic-analysis sharp-constant problem, not an arbitrary polynomial slice. The three-point zero-mean case is L4-isometric, making order five the first nontrivial odd cycle; the exact order-five algebraic constant and exhaustive extremizer orbit establish a sharp benchmark and a two-phase reduction potentially reusable for studying larger odd cycles, including the independently documented order-31 open problem. This is a worthwhile self-contained exact natural invariant without claiming general-N resolution.
residual_risks: No all-odd-order monotonicity, generic-dimensional bound, complex-input norm, or universal consequence is established.
Value concerns a motivated exact first nontrivial finite cyclic case, not a general classification.
